alt: Three panels distinguish renal drug clearance, accumulation in blood and direct kidney tissue injury.

Simplified nephron and collecting-duct pathway: lithium enters through ENaC, reduces the ADH response and water reabsorption, and increases urine output. Chronic tubulointerstitial injury is shown separately.

Thiazides, ACE inhibitors or ARBs, and NSAIDs may raise lithium concentrations. SGLT2 inhibitors may lower concentrations. Amlodipine usually has minimal effect. Medication changes prompt lithium monitoring.

Review draft of separate pregabalin and gabapentin dose-range charts by creatinine clearance, with a separate haemodialysis supplement strip. Values reproduce the existing lesson and await product-specific verification.
Escitalopram, quetiapine, ondansetron and low potassium or magnesium converge on QT prolongation and potential ventricular arrhythmia, prompting ECG, electrolyte and medication review.

CYP3A4 inhibition reduces calcineurin inhibitor metabolism and raises exposure and toxicity risk. Induction increases metabolism and lowers exposure, raising rejection risk. Stopping the interacting drug can reverse the effect.
